notes:
Context: Sundial builds an internal code search + assistant sold to large engineering orgs. Moving from ad-hoc Elastic + custom TF-IDF/LSI to embeddings+rerank. Large, frequently changing repo corpus (approx 120M documents / ~150M embeddings). Key asks: low p50/p95 latency for dev IDE workflows, weekly re-indexing + on-demand repo push, strict SSO/SAML + audit logging, and deterministic fallback for outages.

POC summary:
- 2026-02-19 demo with Priya (AE) + Ethan (SE) + CTO (Ari Novak). Live demo: Redwood hosted API vs in-house Elastic+FAISS baseline on a 10M-sample slice.
- CTO quote: "We need sub-150ms p50 for in-IDE hits, otherwise dev adoption stalls."
- Current infra: Kubernetes on GCP for app layer, artifacts stored in self-hosted Git + GCS; nightly CI triggers re-index jobs (~4x full shards/month).
- Data shape: mix of code files, docstrings, markdown, binary blobs filtered; average vector dim 1536 (open model family), embedding set size grows ~15% month-over-month.
- Cost sensitivity: high — want predictable per-query unit economics; exploring Dedicated vs Private to reduce egress + vector storage costs.
- Reranking: Built-in candidate retrieval from ANN, then lightweight transformer reranker on top for precision in top-5. Interested in Redwood's built-in rerank pipeline and ability to run rerank on cheaper CPU tier.
- Compliance: Need SOC2 + customer audit logs; retention controls for PII removal on request.

Operational notes / shorthand:
- Asked for tech spec comparing batching strategies + KV cache behavior for code contexts (long sequences, large token windows).
- Concern: frequent re-index could blow up write IOPS and cold-cache latency spikes — wants suggested autoscale/backoff patterns.
- Wants traffic shaping: dev IDE calls (low latency, high QPS) vs nightly search bulk jobs (high throughput, lower SLA).

Sales notes:
- Champion: Ari Novak (CTO) - very technical, wants kernel-level explanation of quantization impacts.
- Economic sponsor: VP Eng (Lina Park) — cares about unit cost and predictable commit model.
- Internal procurement timeline: legal + infosec reviews targeted end of March; procurement decision expected early April if POC shows latency + cost numbers.

Stated POC success metrics:
- p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 400ms for single-vector lookup + rerank on demo dataset.
- cost per query (avg) <= $0.004 at current scale projection.
- re-index full-week pipeline completes < 6 hours for 120M-doc corpus (using incremental + shard parallelism).

Notes on demos and artifacts:
- Demo recording: ff-2026-02-19-8a3f2b (linked).
- Sent follow-up email w/ benchmarking ask: thread-4721-ppo-search-poc.
- Shared POC design: drive:/deals/sundial/poc-design-v1.pdf

Short quote from SE after demo: "Baseline FAISS was cheaper per-lookup but latency tail and reindex time are the problem — Redwood's batching + cache algorithms look promising for dev UX."
